thread:
Maya: Heads up — observed recurring latency spikes on the CUTLASS 4-bit path for short sequences (<=32). p95 jumps from ~30ms to ~110ms after enabling the new fp4 kernel. @Liam @Arjun :eyes:
Liam: Which fleet/arch? SM80 or SM90? Could be bank-conflict or a miscompilation.
Arjun: Seen this on ded-gpu-2 (SM80) and a canary on SM90 as well, but pattern differs. SM80 shows big tail, SM90 more consistent but slower overall.
Maya: Repro script attached in thread (quick run):
```bash
python perf_run.py --model tiny --quant 4bit --kernel cutlass --batch 8 --seq 16 --trials 200
```
Maya: Short log snippet:
```
[run 102] latency(ms): mean=28.9 p50=27.4 p95=109.8 p99=154.2
[run 101] latency(ms): mean=29.1 p50=27.5 p95=31.2 p99=36.0
```
Sasha: Interesting — p95 flips between normal and huge across runs. Could be KV-cache alignment/eviction thrash when batcher boundaries hit a different code path. Any KV hit-rate diffs?
Maya: KV hit-rate stable (~82%) across runs. I instrumented KV jitter and saw a correlation with small bursts of kvcache write amplification when CUDA streams reorder.
Liam: Did you try forcing continuous batching (no dynamic population) to rule out batching heuristics?
Maya: Yes — forcing fixed batch of 8 removes spikes. So heuristics + kernel choice + KV caching interaction likely.
Arjun: Plot from profiler (nsight): showed frequent device-to-device memcpy around kernel launch on spiky runs. Also CUTLASS launcher sometimes falls back to a slower kernel when tile alignment mismatch occurs.
Maya: Found a reproducible condition: when request sequence lengths alternate (16, 8,16,8) the CUTLASS 4-bit launcher toggles between optimized-tile kernel and a generic fallback, which forces extra packing/unpacking and flushes small KV pages.
Sasha: That explains why fixed batch removes it — homogeneous shapes avoid toggling.
Liam: Two fixes to consider: 1) tweak batching heuristic to prefer shape-homogeneous grouping (nearby sequences of same seq_len), 2) add a kernel-stability penalty in the prober so we avoid oscillating kernel choices for high-qps endpoints.
Arjun: Also saw that a particular build flag we flipped earlier (-DCUTLASS_USE_LDS_OPT=ON) changes register pressure and made the fallback more likely on SM80. Reverting that flag dropped p95 tails in my local runs.
Maya: Reverted flag in a canary and p95 tails improved, but SM90 still slower overall for fp4. We should gate the flag by arch.
Sasha: Proposed short-term mitigation: prefer INT8/CUTLASS path for heterogeneous short-seq workloads and default to FP8/CUTLASS only for stable shapes. Long-term: improve tile-matching logic in the kernel selector so it predicts instability cost.
Liam: Agree. Also add quick probe telemetry: emit kernel-switch events with reason + prev/next kernel id and KV miss delta. That will help detect oscillations in prod.
Maya: I'll open a small RFC and a perf ticket. Suggest config flags: 
```json
{
  "prober": { "tunable_stability_penalty": 0.15, "homogeneous_batch_window": 120 /* ms */ },
  "build": { "arch_specific_flags": { "SM80": "-DCUTLASS_USE_LDS_OPT=OFF", "SM90": "-DCUTLASS_USE_LDS_OPT=ON" } }
}
```
Arjun: One more datapoint — enabling KV page alignment to 4KB boundaries in the allocator removed the device memcpy spikes in my run. Likely the packer was crossing pages and triggering extra DMA.
Sasha: Nice catch. That suggests a runtime improvement: align small KV allocations and avoid cross-page writes when using quantized packers. Add a unit test for allocator alignment + packer interaction.
Maya: Action items:
- Maya: RFC + perf ticket with repro and canary results (will attach nsight traces)
- Liam: Add kernel-switch telemetry and a prober metric for stability (ETA 3d)
- Arjun: Experiment with arch-gated build flags and KV allocator alignment patch (ETA 2d)
- Sasha: Batching heuristic tweak POC to prefer homogeneous grouping (ETA 4d)
- infra-bot: create canary for ded-gpu-2 and a SM90 node pool run.
infra-bot: Canary created: canary/ded-gpu-2/quant-probe-1794123456, runs scheduled across SM80/SM90 pools.
Liam: Also note — regression might have been introduced by the fp4 quant encoder change on 1794000000 build. Will bisect if needed.
Maya: Thanks all — let's sync tomorrow 10am to review canary results. :thumbsup:
